doc: twoody/login-approver/v1 — which device approved a computer's login (`twoody-server login`), proved so that the account cannot put its own approver key in its place. Reference: src/vault/contracts.ts loginApproverProof.

The computer's console shows, with the user code, a one-time secret the account never sees: 12 characters of Crockford's base32 alphabet '0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ' (60 bits), written 'XXXX-XXXX-XXXX'. The person types (or scans) it on the approving Twoody Desktop or phone.

Reading the secret: upper-case it, drop '-' and spaces, read O as 0 and I or L as 1; it must then be 12 characters of the alphabet. Reading the user code: upper-case, O as 0, I or L as 1, keep [0-9A-Z], 8 characters, written 'XXXX-XXXX'.

proof = lowercase hex of HMAC-SHA256(key = the secret's 12 characters as UTF-8, message = canonical header of the label 'twoody/login-approver/v1' then the fields [1, user code 'XXXX-XXXX', approver public key (64 lowercase hex), the computer's tunnel public key (64 lowercase hex, GET /computer_logins/:code tunnel_public_key)]). Canonical header: the label's UTF-8 bytes, then each field as UTF-8 of String(field) prefixed by its length on two bytes, big-endian (as the vault statements).

The approving device sends it as approver.proof with POST /computer_logins/:code/approve; the account hands it back with the approved poll; the computer pins the approver key only when the proof holds for its own secret, code and tunnel key.
